title: Counterspy
paragraphs: An espionage and counterintelligence series centered on agent David Harding and his fight against enemy spies, saboteurs, and organized threats to the United States.

Long-running espionage and national-security drama created by Phillips H. Lord. Don MacLaughlin’s David Harding leads the fictional United States Counterspies, with Mandel Kramer’s Harry Peters prominent in surviving postwar episodes. Plot emphasis shifts from Axis espionage during World War II toward Cold War and broader security/crime threats after the war.

GRH documents the program through Blue Network era (May 18, 1942 to June 14, 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], ABC era (June 15, 1945 to August 31, 1950) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], NBC era (October 13, 1950 to September 24, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Mutual era (October 5, 1953 to November 29, 1957) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|mandel-kramer|Mandel Kramer]] (performer on 60 recordings), [[person|don-maclaughlin|Don MacLaughlin]] (performer on 59 recordings), Phillips H. Lord (producer on 57 recordings), Jesse Crawford (organ on 26 recordings, organist on 5 recordings, and music on 1 recording), Marx B. Loeb (director on 18 recordings), Edward Adamson (writer on 10 recordings and performer on 1 recording), and Leonard L. Bass (director on 11 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include espionage and counterintelligence, robbery, theft and stolen valuables, rackets and organized crime, sabotage, bombs and destructive subversion, smuggling, black markets and untaxed trade, and counterfeiting and financial fraud.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including World War II counterintelligence drama, Postwar and Cold War national-security shift, Broader crime and security cases, and Blue/ABC to NBC to Mutual migration.
